## NO-SCALE-BACK RAMP (2026-09-26, Nolan: never scale back, always retry, ramp weekly)

Nolan's binding order 2026-09-26: on social, a failed pass is retried, never answered with lower caps. Failure means do it again. This pass: every 2h, caps 75 likes + 20 comments per pass. Weekly ramp RESUMED: +5 likes/week and +3 comments/week from these caps, no ceiling. A hard platform block (checkpoint/action block) stops the pass and is surfaced; once clear, resume at the ramped caps, never at minimum, never a hold period. Guard, intent-ledger, and fail-closed rules below are unchanged.

Run one Facebook engagement pass via ~/workspace/pig-fb/run_pass.sh (heavy Facebook volume: ramp schedule in the body below; see the engagement-format preference in AGENTS.md and Facebook comment voice rules); run it once (dispatch returns immediately with a receipt; outcome recording is owned by the facebook-engagement-collect schedule), verify, log to the daily memory note under the dated FB Pass heading.

Facebook engagement for PING Social outreach (2026-09-23, per Nolan's binding order; accelerated 2026-09-23 ~13:52 MDT, comment ramp added ~13:54 MDT; throttle LIFTED 2026-09-26 per Nolan's no-scale-back order): per pass 75 likes + 20 comments on local business/community feed posts in Mesa County, every 2h. Weekly ramp: +5 likes/week and +3 comments/week from these caps, no ceiling (2026-09-26). A checkpoint, warning, or restriction stops the pass and is surfaced to Nolan; the next pass resumes at the ramped caps. Never halve caps, never drop to minimum, never hold. Every action against a LOCAL business Page is eligible: services, trades, home services, retail, restaurants, agriculture, professional services (see ~/workspace/outreach/facebook-engagement.md). Local non-profit and community organization pages are eligible for likes only, no comments. Do NOT like/comment personal profiles of non-friends; only engage public Page posts, never friends-only or non-public posts. Also eligible: Facebook friend posts. Comments must be punchy and short (under 20 words), expert/techy but down to earth and funny. Never selling, never PING mention, no links, no contact info, business Pages only, never personal profiles. 60-120s pacing between actions (human cadence). Prefer regular feed posts over reels; only comment a reel if it already has public comments. Stop instantly on any action block or checkpoint and log it. All engagement lives under ~/workspace/outreach/, especially facebook-engagement.md (history, candidates, pass log). NEVER ask for confirmation (perpetual mode); stay silent unless something genuinely needs Nolan's call, e.g. a checkpoint, warning, account restriction, or a reply from a business owner. Surface only real anomalies.

- DEGRADED-PROBE GATE (2026-09-26, Nolan-approved; URL-injection fallback route added 2026-09-26 per Nolan's do-it-again order): run `python3 ~/workspace/outreach/fb-degraded-probe.py` FIRST, before any discovery. Exit 0 = run normal discovery below. Exit 2 = probe failed, outage continues: do NOT end the pass; route to the URL-injection fallback instead: run `python3 ~/workspace/outreach/fb-url-fallback.py --pool ~/workspace/outreach/fb-url-candidates.json` (read-only `post read --url` validation of genuinely-observed URLs with recorded acquisition sources; never guesses post IDs; drops unresolvable URLs; drops ledger-blocked posts (open intents, terminal UNKNOWNs, prior engagement) at build time; half caps 37 likes + 10 comments until its trust gate reports full caps unlocked). If it exits 0, it prints a JSON summary with the validated job path: continue with the never-reengage filter + dispatch steps below using that job file (already in /tmp/fb-job-<timestamp>.json format; the guard, intent-ledger write-intents/mark-execution, and driver all apply unchanged), log the pass section as FALLBACK (note the caps level, trust streak, and acquisition_source=url-injection), and record the outcome as `--record-outcome stefi-outage` after dispatch (preferred path still down; engagement happened via fallback; stefi returns ONLY on a successful probe, never on elapsed time). If it exits 2 (pool/ledger/CLI infra failure) or 3 (pool empty or nothing validated/eligible), append a cheap pass section to ~/workspace/outreach/facebook-engagement.md ("NOT_ATTEMPTED, degraded probe failed and fallback yielded nothing: <reason from the summary>"), do NOT run run_pass.sh, do NOT touch the intent ledger, record `--record-outcome stefi-outage`, end. After a normal (non-fallback) pass completes, record the outcome: `python3 ~/workspace/outreach/fb-degraded-probe.py --record-outcome ok` on a completed pass, `--record-outcome stefi-outage` when the pass is NOT_ATTEMPTED due to the stefi 500 + timeline 403 signature, `--record-outcome other` for any other failure mode.
- Job file: build /tmp/fb-job-<timestamp>.json with the CANONICAL builder only: `python3 ~/workspace/outreach/build-fb-job.py <pass-number>` (pass-parameterized, 2026-09-28 consolidation; includes the evidence-trained CURATED_DROP_RE qualifier from curated passes 129-139). Do NOT create per-pass build-fbNNN-job.py scripts; the old ones are retired shims or historical artifacts. Build from the candidate pool in ~/workspace/outreach/facebook-engagement.md (75 likes + 20 comments in the standard format) and run the never-reengage filter first: `python3 ~/workspace/outreach/never_reengage.py --filter-job /tmp/fb-job-<timestamp>.json --history ~/workspace/outreach/facebook-engagement.md --output /tmp/fb-job-<timestamp>.json --prune-if-empty`. The filter also strips actions whose URLs are malformed or already handled. Every action's "page" field must be UNIQUE per post within the job; never reuse a generic descriptor like "Group (photo post)" for multiple posts (2026-09-18: the guard's within-pass dedup keys on the "page" string, so all but the first duplicate are stripped). Use a distinctive descriptor per post: content snippet, business name, or post ID.
- Execute: run `~/workspace/pig-fb/run_pass.sh /tmp/fb-job-<timestamp>.json`. It runs the never-re-engage guard first, then copies the filtered job to the Pig and launches the detached engagement worker there (60-120s human pacing between actions), then returns IMMEDIATELY with a dispatch receipt JSON. It does NOT wait for the pass and prints no action results. If the guard reports blocked actions, copy the SKIPPED_REENGAGEMENT / BLOCKED reasons into your pass log section. Outcome recording is asynchronous and NOT this pass's job: the worker appends one fsync'd progress line per completed action to the Pig inbox, and the facebook-engagement-collect schedule (every 15 minutes) downloads result/progress files and records each action's OBSERVATION into the intent ledger. Never re-run run_pass.sh to "check on" a dispatched pass; the collector owns collection, and the in-flight guard refuses a second worker while one runs.
- Infra outcomes: if run_pass.sh exits 2 (Pig unreachable, CDP down, a previous worker still in flight, or guard fail-closed), end the run with no user-facing message and note it in the log. (Dispatch returns immediately, so there is no result to wait for and no result timeout. If the worker later reports logged_out, the collector records the pass as NOT_ATTEMPTED.) If the Pig Chrome window was closed or the Pig rebooted, Nolan must log in again; do not message Nolan about it, just note "Pig Facebook session needs Nolan login" in the pass log.
- Post-pass verification: read the result and confirm observed > 0; note exact counts in the log. Append a pass log section to ~/workspace/outreach/facebook-engagement.md ("## FB Pass <timestamp>": eligible/blocked counts, pass_id, dispatched/receipt, notes). If logged_in false or observed == 0 with actions attempted, note the suspected cause and next step.
- ACTION INTENT (2026-09-14, states per Nolan's directive: ACTION_INTENT_DURABLE -> EXECUTION -> OBSERVATION -> FINALIZATION; terminals EXECUTED/FAILED/UNKNOWN_EXECUTION/NOT_ATTEMPTED): run_pass.sh writes one intent record per action to ~/workspace/outreach/action-intent-ledger.jsonl BEFORE anything is copied to the Pig, marks EXECUTION only after the job is delivered to the Pig (2026-09-24 orphan model: dispatch separated from collection), and the 15-minute collector records each action's observation from the worker's result/progress files (EXECUTED/FAILED) or from proven non-execution (NOT_ATTEMPTED). (2026-09-15, Nolan's directive): the intent ledger is now the canonical pipeline sink for Facebook DMs; keep it authoritative and reconcile against facebook-engagement.md at least every pass.
- Parallelism: run through run_pass.sh once per pass; never two concurrent jobs on this account (interleaved actions break pacing and risk blocks). The in-flight guard enforces this mechanically: dispatch exits 2 if any fb-profile worker (engage.js, fb-unfollow.js, meta-ask.js) is already running on the Pig, and the collector never launches workers. Also never overlap with the Instagram engagement pass (same person visible across platforms), even though it uses a different account; stagger by at least 30 minutes. (2026-09-23, per Nolan)

FOCUS — DO NOT START AN IDENTITY REWRITE.

THE IDENTITY FORENSIC IS COMPLETE ENOUGH.

Preserve the proven semantic boundaries.
Preserve existing IDs.
Do not remint.
Do not deploy constitutional-runtime merely to satisfy architectural purity.
Do not add PostgreSQL identity persistence unless a real product invariant requires it.
Do not collapse workflow/provider/caller/owner identifiers into entity identity.

Most importantly:

DO NOT BLOCK FYD ON IDENTITY CONVERGENCE.

============================================================
NEW TARGET: MAKE THE FYD BACKEND OPERABLE
============================================================

HARVEST THE MOST IMPORTANT EXISTING PING MISSION CONTROL,
OBSERVABILITY, MISSION, RUN, EXECUTION, EVENT, EVIDENCE, AND AGENT
COMPONENTS.

WIRE THEM INTO THE FYD PIPELINE.

DO NOT BUILD A SECOND MISSION CONTROL.

DO NOT PORT THE OLD UI WHOLESALE.

HARVEST THE OPERATIONAL PRIMITIVES.

============================================================
PRODUCT REASON
============================================================

FYD is becoming a compiler/runtime:

SOURCE
→ ACQUIRE
→ OBSERVE
→ EVIDENCE
→ OBJECT GRAPH
→ SITE SPEC
→ RENDER
→ ASK FYD
→ PROPOSAL
→ APPROVAL
→ REGENERATION.

We now need to SEE AND OPERATE THIS PIPELINE.

Mission Control should become the operational projection over that exact
system.

NOT another product.

============================================================
SEARCH FIRST
============================================================

Search all PING/CascadeProjects/history/docs for existing:

Mission Control
missions
runs
executions
workers

activity timelines.

LIVE
PROVEN BUT UNWIRED
UI-ONLY
MOCK
DUPLICATE
DEAD
UNSAFE
HARVEST.

Do not trust screenshots or component names.

TRACE CALL GRAPHS.

============================================================
HARVEST BACKEND BEFORE UI
============================================================

We care first about executable primitives such as:

MissionRuntime
MissionScheduler
ExecutionAuthority
ExecutionAdapter
UnifiedEventRuntime
ping_events
projection/replay
artifact/evidence handling
capability evaluation
agent execution
approval transitions
health/runtime status.

Reuse what is proven.

Wrap what has incompatible interfaces.

Do not rewrite working machinery merely because FYD naming differs.

============================================================
FYD PIPELINE → MISSION MODEL
============================================================

Do NOT make every function call a mission.

Use missions for meaningful user/system objectives.

Example:

MISSION
Build FYD for Coppersmith

RUN
Observation/regeneration attempt

STAGES

ACQUIRE
EXTRACT
RESOLVE
PROJECT
PLAN
RENDER
VERIFY.

Each stage should expose:

status
started_at
finished_at
input references
output references
evidence
error
retryability.

This gives us operational truth without creating another workflow engine.

============================================================
OBSERVABILITY MODEL
============================================================

For one FYD generation I want to inspect:

MISSION
  └── RUN
       ├── source observation
       ├── extraction
       │    └── 38 facts
       ├── object projection
       │    └── 4 objects / 3 relationships
       ├── SiteSpec generation
       │    └── digest
       ├── rendering
       ├── verification
       └── result.

Clicking a stage should expose evidence already generated by the system.

DO NOT create a second logging universe.

Project from existing mission/event/evidence state.

============================================================
THE UI TO HARVEST
============================================================

Search the old Mission Control UI and harvested UI documentation.

Take ONLY components/patterns that help operate FYD:

mission/run list
pipeline/stage visualization
status badges
event/activity timeline
artifact/evidence viewer
object inspector
relationship inspector
agent activity
proposal/approval view
failure/retry view
health indicators.

Do not import:

mock dashboards
decorative metrics
unused navigation
Linear imitation for its own sake
constitutional jargon customers/operators don't need.

============================================================
MISSION CONTROL INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE
============================================================

Keep it brutally small initially:

OVERVIEW

MISSIONS

OBJECTS

EVIDENCE

AGENTS

EVENTS

SYSTEM.

A mission opens into its RUN.

A run shows its PIPELINE.

A pipeline stage links to the actual objects/evidence/events it produced.

============================================================
OBJECT INSPECTOR
============================================================

This is high leverage.

Select any FYD object and show:

ID
schema/type
controller/owner where applicable
current projection
relationships
source evidence
visibility
generated-site usage
available capabilities
event history.

This becomes the engineering version of:

WHY THIS?

Same substrate.

Different projection.

============================================================
EVIDENCE INSPECTOR
============================================================

For a fact show:

VALUE
SOURCE
SOURCE OBJECT
OBSERVED AT
METHOD
DIRECT / DERIVED / INFERRED
CURRENT / SUPERSEDED
OBJECTS USING IT.

This should use existing evidence/provenance structures.

No parallel provenance model.

============================================================
SITE INSPECTOR
============================================================

For each generated FYD site show:

SiteSpec digest
source graph digest
pages
sections
object bindings
owner overrides
generated presentation
last regeneration
next detected source changes.

This will make regeneration debugging dramatically faster.

============================================================
AGENT INSPECTOR
============================================================

Show:

agent
mission
run
allowed capabilities
context references
proposal
approval requirement
result
evidence.

NEVER display raw secrets/provider credentials/private keys.

Agent output remains proposal/evidence until authorized canonical
transition.

============================================================
OBSERVABILITY MUST BE EVENT-DRIVEN
============================================================

Do not instrument FYD with hundreds of bespoke dashboard callbacks.

Prefer existing canonical/operational events.

Mission Control consumes/project them.

Conceptually:

FYD ACTION
→ EXISTING AUTHORITY
→ EVENT
→ PROJECTION
→ MISSION CONTROL.

Not:

FYD ACTION
→ SPECIAL MC DATABASE WRITE.

Mission Control is a projection.

============================================================
DO NOT CONFUSE THESE STATES
============================================================

MISSION STATE != OBJECT STATE

RUN STATE != CANONICAL TRUTH

EXECUTION != AUTHORIZATION

AGENT OUTPUT != APPROVED TRANSITION

MISSION CONTROL != AUTHORITY

DASHBOARD != DATABASE OF RECORD.

Preserve those boundaries.

============================================================
FAILURE TAXONOMY
============================================================

Reuse existing typed failures where available.

At minimum the operational surface needs to distinguish:

PENDING
RUNNING
SUCCEEDED
FAILED
BLOCKED
UNKNOWN.

For stage failures preserve:

code
message
retryable
evidence reference.

No giant stack dump as the product model.

============================================================
RETRY
============================================================

Retry must operate on the failed operation/stage where safe.

Do not regenerate everything merely because rendering failed.

Example:

ACQUIRE PASS
EXTRACT PASS
OBJECTS PASS
SITESPEC PASS
RENDER FAIL

Retry:

RENDER

using the immutable/referenced prior outputs.

This is one reason observability matters.

============================================================
FYD PRODUCT LOOP REMAINS P0
============================================================

DO NOT stop the product lane.

The next user-visible boundary remains:

RENDERED FYD
→ ASK FYD
→ EVIDENCE.

Mission Control work runs in support of that loop.

The first operational mission worth displaying should be a REAL FYD
generation.

============================================================
ASK FYD SHOULD CREATE OBSERVABLE WORK
============================================================

Example:

"What services does this company offer and how do you know?"

Mission Control should allow us to inspect:

question
resolved FYD identity
objects selected
evidence selected
agent/model invocation if any
answer
citations/evidence refs
duration
failure if applicable.

But do not log private prompts/context indiscriminately.

Store safe references/metadata where possible.

============================================================
SITE CUSTOMIZATION SHOULD ALSO BE OBSERVABLE
============================================================

"Move emergency plumbing to the top."

MISSION/RUN:

interpret request
→ generate SitePatch
→ validate bindings
→ capability check
→ await approval
→ apply
→ regenerate
→ verify.

Mission Control should show exactly where it is.

THIS is useful Mission Control.

============================================================
NO NEW AUTHORITIES
============================================================

Do not invent:

ObservabilityAuthority
MissionControlAuthority
PipelineAuthority
SiteAuthority
AgentDashboardAuthority.

Use existing:

mission
execution
event
capability
evidence
projection primitives.

============================================================
IDENTITY DECISION
============================================================

The forensic discovered a critical distinction.

GOOD.

FREEZE IT.

Kernel JS stable identity semantics remain protected.

Constitutional compatibility semantics remain protected.

Python UUIDv7 remains unique execution/work identity where proven.

Provider identities remain claims/provider references.

Workflow IDs remain workflow IDs.

Owner authentication remains authentication.

Do not normalize these merely because they contain the word identity.

The uploaded forensic's proposed constitutional survivor is NOT a reason
to immediately deploy a dormant subsystem.

A dormant authority with placeholder crypto is not automatically more
authoritative than the proven live path.

Call graph + persisted compatibility + actual runtime usage win.

============================================================
HARVEST LAW
============================================================

For every Mission Control component:

SOURCE
PURPOSE
LIVE CALLERS
DEPENDENCIES
DATA SOURCE
AUTHORITY OR PROJECTION
KEEP / WRAP / REJECT
FYD USE
TEST.

Maintain the lightweight harvest manifest.

We want:

SMALL CODE
BIG OPERATIONAL LEVERAGE.

============================================================
FIRST IMPLEMENTATION
